verdict: Micron's revenue rose 84% from a year ago to a record $8.71B as AI data centers devoured its memory chips, and a gross margin that was negative a year earlier swung to 38% — delivering $1.87B of profit.

takeaways.title: Data centers became the majority
takeaways.text: Data-center revenue passed half of all sales for the first time, growing more than 40% in a single quarter and over 400% from a year ago. AI servers need DRAM and HBM in quantities consumer devices never did.

takeaways.title: Margins snapped back
takeaways.text: Gross margin hit 38.4%, from −0.7% a year earlier, as memory prices kept recovering from the 2023 crash. In memory chips, price — not volume — is the profit lever, and it swung Micron from a $1.23B loss to a $1.87B profit.

takeaways.title: Spending heavily to keep up
takeaways.text: Capital spending of $3.13B nearly matched the $3.24B of cash the operations generated, leaving adjusted free cash flow of just $112M — record profits, but almost all of them reinvested in new capacity.

footerNote: Business-unit revenues are on Micron's recast segment basis (adopted in fiscal 2026), derived from the segment note of Micron's Q2 FY26 Form 10-Q (six months ended February 2025, less the quarter ended February 2025); 'All other' is the small residual outside the four units. Reported operating income was $2,174M; the chart shows Micron's $2M net 'other operating income' credit in the other-income step rather than as a negative expense, so chart operating income is $2,172M — net income is unchanged.
